title: Pacer
subtitle: min per mark
help:
Pacer
Times a practice paper against a plan.

1. Enter minutes, marks and the
   checkpoint size.
2. EXE starts the clock.
3. F1 logs a mark, F2 pauses.

The gap line says how far ahead or
behind the plan you are.

Keys: EXE start/stop, F1 mark, F2
pause, F3 finish, EXIT back.

title: Cards
subtitle: flashcards
help:
Cards
Flashcards with a Leitner schedule.

A deck is one file in Bench/cards,
one card per line:
   question | answer

Right answers move a card to the
next box, wrong ones send it back.
Progress is saved when the session
ends, never during it.

Keys: EXE reveal/mark, F1 right,
F2 wrong, EXIT back.

title: Notes
subtitle: Markdown
help:
Notes
Reads .md and .txt from Bench/notes.

Markdown headings, lists, quotes,
bold and code are drawn in the
palette. Long lines wrap; the wrap
width is a setting.

Keys: UP/DOWN scroll, EXE page down,
ALPHA search, F2 headings, EXIT.

title: Study log
subtitle: minutes per day
help:
Study log
What you did, for how long, and
on which day, in a text file you
can also edit by hand:

  2026-10-31 25 pacer

A broken line is skipped and
counted, never added up wrongly.

F1 adds a session: type the
minutes, UP/DOWN picks the tool,
LEFT/RIGHT moves between the three
fields, EXE saves it. F2 deletes
the last one, which is the mistake
you will make.

Bench cannot read the calendar, so
a new entry takes the day after the
newest one in the log; UP/DOWN on
the day moves it. The file is
written once, when you leave.

title: Complex
subtitle: a + bi
help:
Complex numbers
Two numbers a and b, one operation
at a time.

F2 picks the operation: a + b,
a - b, a x b, a / b and a ^ n, where
n is the real part of b.

The result is written three ways:
rectangular (-1 + 2i), its modulus
and argument, and polar form.

F3 shows the argument in degrees,
F4 in radians.

Keys: arrows move, digits type,
DEL deletes, F1 clears, EXIT home.

title: Function
subtitle: x and f(x)
help:
Function table
A table and a value for f(x).

1. Pick a slot f, g, h, p, q, r.
2. EXE types the expression on the
   keyboard: x, pi, e, + - * / ^,
   sin cos tan ln log sqrt abs.
3. F1 opens the table.

In the table: LEFT/RIGHT move the
start, F1 changes the step, F2 the
row count, EXE probes one value.
F4 switches degrees and radians;
the mode shows in the title bar.

Slots are written to
Bench/state/exprs.txt when you
leave the tool.

Keys: EXE edit, F1 table, F3 clear.

title: Sequences
subtitle: terms, sums
help:
Sequences
Arithmetic and geometric terms,
their sums, and binomials.

Three screens, F4 next and F3 back.

  Arithmetic  a, d, n: the nth term
              and the sum, then the
              first few terms.
  Geometric   a, r, n: as above, plus
              the sum to infinity when
              |r| < 1.
  Binomial    n choose k exactly, and
              row n of Pascal.

Terms count from 1, so the first term
is n = 1.  C(n,k) is refused rather
than rounded when it passes 64 bits.

Keys: arrows move, digits type,
EXE solves, F1 clears.

title: Polynomials
subtitle: roots, expand
help:
Polynomials
Quadratics, expansion and rational
roots.

Three screens, F4 or F2 next and F3
back:
  Quadratic  a, b, c give the
             discriminant, both roots
             and the vertex.
  Expand     (ax + b)^n to degree 8.
  Roots      c0..cn as coefficients;
             whole and half roots are
             found, the rest is shown.

Arrows move between fields, digits
type, DEL deletes, F1 clears.  F2 on
the roots screen adds a coefficient.

Rounding is half up on the digits.

title: Root finder
subtitle: bisect, Newton
help:
Root finder
Solves f(x) = 0 one step at a time,
so the convergence is visible.

F2 picks the method:
  bisection needs a and b with a
    sign change between them
  Newton needs one guess x0
  secant needs two guesses x0, x1

F3 solves. The table lists n, x and
f(x); the plot marks every iterate.

Radians always, whatever the angle
setting says. Tolerance 1e-6, at most
50 steps.

F4 lists the last eight answers, so a
root does not vanish when the fields
change. Nothing is written to storage.

Keys: EXE edits f or solves, F1 clears,
F2 method, F4 history, arrows move
and scroll.

title: Triangle
subtitle: sides, angles
help:
Triangle
Three sides and three angles. Fill
in what you know and leave the rest
blank.

Give any three values, at least one
a side: SSS, SAS, ASA and AAS all
solve, and the fields fill in.

SSA - two sides and an angle not
between them - can have two answers.
The title bar then says so and F2
swaps between the two triangles.

Area and perimeter are under the
fields.  F3 degrees, F4 radians.

Keys: arrows move, digits type,
EXE solves, F1 clears.

title: Base and bits
subtitle: hex, shifts
help:
Bases and bits
One number in base 2 to 36, and
the same number as two's complement
at 8, 16 and 32 bits.

F1 switches between converting
and the bitwise operators.

F3 changes the entry base, or the
operator: AND, OR, XOR, shift left
and shift right. A shift uses the
count in b and refuses 63 or more.

F2 opens the letter keyboard for
digits above 9, since the keypad
has no A to F keys this add-in may
count on. Digits can still be
typed straight in.

Keys: digits type, DEL takes one
back, F4 swaps a and b.

title: Number theory
subtitle: gcd to CRT
help:
Number theory
Nine functions, each with working.

gcd, lcm, prime test, factorise,
modular inverse, CRT, divisors,
totient and base conversion.

Factorisation shows a progress bar;
EXIT cancels it.

Keys: UP/DOWN choose, EXE open,
EXIT back.

title: Statistics
subtitle: mean to regression
help:
Statistics
Type a value, press EXE to add it,
and the summary is worked out as
you go. Up to 200 values.

F2 switches between one list and
paired data (x, then y). Pairs give
the line y = a + bx, r and r squared.

F3 picks the quartile method:
  median  halves split through the
          median
  sheet   (n-1)p + 1, interpolated

F4 shows the working for the standard
deviation. F1 clears the list.

Keys: digits type, EXE adds, DEL takes
back a digit or a value.

title: Lab graph
subtitle: error bars
help:
Lab graph
Type a measured pair and its error,
press EXE, and repeat. F2 draws
the graph with a bar up and down
through every point and the line of
best fit.

The gradient comes with its standard
error, from the residuals, and r
squared says how well the line
fits. Fewer than three points leave
nothing to measure the error against,
so it is left off.

The axes hold the whole bar, not
just the centre, so a measurement
never runs off the top.

Up to twelve points. F1 clears,
F3 puts the example back, DEL on an
empty field drops the last point.

Keys: digits type, LEFT/RIGHT pick
a field, EXE adds the point.

title: Uncertainty
subtitle: value and error
help:
Uncertainty
Arithmetic with errors, to 1 or 2
significant figures.

Type a value and its absolute error,
pick an operation, type the second
value and error.

Chain mode keeps the result as the
first value of the next step.

Keys: F1..F3 operation, EXE apply,
EXIT back.

title: Sig figs
subtitle: round, standard
help:
Sig figs
How many figures, and how to write
them.

UP/DOWN picks a mode, LEFT/RIGHT
changes n, EXE types the number.

Count: leading zeros never count,
and trailing zeros count only after
a decimal point. 0.004560 has 4.

Round: half up on the decimal
digits, so 1234.5 to 3 figures is
1230 = 1.23 x 10^3.

Practice asks a question; type the
count and EXE marks it, F2 moves
on.

Keys: EXE type, F1 clear.

title: SUVAT
subtitle: motion, projectiles
help:
SUVAT and projectiles
Type any three of s, u, v, a and t.
The other two are worked out, with
the equation that gave each one.

Use the arrows to pick a quantity,
type the number, press EXE. DEL on
an empty field un-knows it.

F2 draws the flight path: range,
greatest height and time in the air
for a launch speed, angle and height.

F3 switches g between 9.81 and 10.
Where a quadratic gives two times,
the first is shown and the second
is mentioned under it.

Keys: digits type, EXE keeps, DEL
takes back, F1 starts again.

title: Moles
subtitle: mass, gas, conc
help:
Moles and solutions
Five calculations, one per mode:
moles from a mass, concentration,
the gas equation, dilution, and
yield or atom economy.

Each mode opens on a worked
example; F1 puts it back.

The unit under each number is the
one the formula wants: volumes in
dm3, so 25 cm3 is 0.025, and
temperature in kelvin.

R is 8.314, for p in kPa and V in
dm3. A zero where a formula divides
says so instead of printing an
infinity.

Keys: UP/DOWN pick a field, digits
type, F3/F4 change mode, DEL takes
a digit back.

title: Settings
subtitle: options
help:
Settings
Five rows: uncertainty figures, the
Pacer checkpoint size, the Notes
wrap width, the unit the Triangle
tool opens in, and whether the
first-run line on the home screen
has been read.

Every value is also a line in
Bench/state/settings.cfg, one per
line, safe to edit by hand.

The file is written only when a
value changes.

Keys: UP/DOWN choose, LEFT/RIGHT
change, EXIT back.

title: About
subtitle: version
help:
About
Version, build date, target and the
storage Bench uses.

Bench never reads or changes Exam
Mode. If the calculator is in Exam
Mode the add-in does not run at
all; that is the OS, not us.
